It is known that at the same moment, balls a and b respectively start from rest at points A and B and move along the smooth inclined straight tracks AM and BM to point M; ball c falls freely from point C to point M. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is a vertical wall, and the bottom is a horizontal plane; a fixed circular ring is in a vertical plane, and the circular ring is tangent to the horizontal plane at the lower point M and tangent to the vertical wall at the left point A. The center C is marked inside the circular ring, located directly above point M and directly to the right of point A. There is also a point B on the wall, located above A, and two smooth straight tracks AM and BM leading to M are drawn in the figure, among which BM is steeper than AM; the problem gives that BM and the horizontal plane make an angle of 60°. Reasoning: Let the radius of the circular ring be R. Since the circular ring is simultaneously tangent to the vertical wall at point A and tangent to the horizontal plane at point M, the distances from the center C to the wall and to the ground are both R, so the height of A above the ground is R, and the vertical height from C to M is also R. From the geometric relationship, the horizontal distance between A and M is R, and the vertical height difference is R, so the angle between AM and the horizontal plane is 45°, and the length of AM is s_a=√2R. Ball a slides down along AM from rest, and the acceleration along the inclined plane is a_a=g sin45°=g/√2, so t_a=√(2s_a/a_a)=√(2√2R/(g/√2))=2√(R/g). Point B is on the wall, BM and the horizontal plane make an angle of 60°, and the horizontal distance from M to the wall is R, so the length of BM is s_b=R/cos60°=2R, and the height of B is R tan60°=√3R. Ball b slides down along BM, and the acceleration is a_b=g sin60°=√3g/2, so t_b=√(2s_b/a_b)=√(4R/(√3g/2))=√(8R/(√3g)). Ball c falls freely from point C to point M, and the falling height is R, so t_c=√(2R/g). Compare the coefficients of the three times: the coefficient of t_c is √2, the coefficient of t_a is 2, and the coefficient of t_b is √(8/√3). Because √2<2<√(8/√3), ball c takes the shortest time and reaches point M first. Final answer: ball c reaches point M first.
